html.body: Date: 2025-04-11 REMARKSThe Advisory Action dated March 26, 2025 and the Final Office Action dated January 27, 2025 has been carefully reviewed. Claims 1 and 16 have been amended. Claims 1-2 and 9-16 are now pending in this application. Favorable consideration and allowance of this application is respectfully requested in light of the following amendments and remarks.I. Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §112 Claims 1 and 16 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter of the invention.A. Artificial Intelligence Software The Examiner has contended that the capabilities of an "artificial intelligence (AI) software" are unclear and requests correction/clarification thereof. See Office Action, p. 3.In light of the discussion with the Examiner in the Examiner Interview of March 13, 2025, Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 16 to call for a "software" as opposed to an "artificial intelligence software". Meanwhile, Paragraphs [0068], [0087], and [0108] of the as- published application described capabilities of the software in the present application.In light of the above, Applicant contends that claims 1 and 16 are properly definite and satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. §112(b). As such, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. §112(b), along with all claims depending therefrom.B. Pre-Known Knowledge The Examiner further contends that it is not clear what a "pre-known knowledge" specifically is and what it encompasses and requests correction/clarification thereof. See Office Action, p. 3.As discussed in the Examiner Interview of March 13, 2025, Applicant has amended claims 1 and 16 to further clarify and define "pre-known knowledge" as including "previous directions and configuration and/or shape of the satellite system." Support for the amendment can be found in Paragraphs [0068] and [0108] of the as-published application.In light of the above, Applicant contends that claims 1 and 16 are properly definite and satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. §112(b). As such, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. §112(b), along with all claims depending therefrom.II. Conclusion In light of the amendments and remarks above, Applicant believes the application is in condition for allowance.A fee in the amount of $1,144 for a Request for Continued Examination for a small entity is being paid herewith. No other fees are believed due with this communication. However, should the Examiner consider any fees to be payable in conjunction with this or any future communication, the Director is authorized to charge any fees or credit any overpayment in connection with this or any future communication to Deposit Account No. 50-1170.Recognizing that Internet communication are not secure, I hereby authorize the USPTO to communicate with the undersigned and practitioners in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33 and 37 CFR 1.34 concerning any subject matter of this application by video conference, instant messaging, or electronic mail. I understand that a copy of these communications will be made of record in the application file.Respectfully submitted, /Mitchell J. Stock/ Mitchell J.
